doc.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Statesmen personnel and Jerry Jerome
summary: Talk about the Statesmen's ages, Jerry Jerome's poor health, and a Bill Kirchner radio profile of Johnny Mandel mentioning Jerome.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So Earl May’s on the gig too, right?
You’ll be one of the younger guys.
The last time I played with them I was the young guy. No I think there’s somebody from Florida who’s not familiar to me. He may be younger than I am. If he is I’ll kill him.
Not Jerry Jerome, he’s older than you.

No this guy’s going to take Jerry’s place. Jerry I understand — Jerry is not too well. It’s odd that you’d mention that, because I have a tape, a jazz profile that Bill Kirchner put together on Johnny Mandel. It was broadcast over National Public Radio. A fine tape. Johnny Mandel and I used to be roommates with Count Basie’s band. Anyway, on this tape he mentions Jerry Jerome and Jerry Jerome’s affiliation with bebop. Because there were a lot of guys in it. I mean this, see—

And since then I’ve talked with Jimmy Owens and he said the New School has some of Jerry Jerome’s arrangements. So I hope to make a copy of this tape and take it to him because I understand he’s not too well.
